# HDateRangePicker

> Two date pickers with start/end constraints and native form validation.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.1. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HDateRangePicker` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-date-range-picker>`.
- Constructor: `HearthDateRangePickerElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HDateRangePicker.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Added in v0.5.0. Two date fields with calendar popovers, not a continuous multi-month selection surface. Model is [start,end]; empty values are empty strings.
- Native form submission uses the same name twice, in start/end order; use FormData.getAll(name). Crossed dates fail validity rather than being silently swapped. min/max apply to both endpoints; required applies to each.

## Public API

modelValue, value: DateRange · label, name, min, max, locale, startLabel, endLabel: string · weekStartsOn: 0 | 1 · required, disabled: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    modelValue?: DateRange;
    value?: DateRange;
    label: string;
    name?: string;
    min?: string;
    max?: string;
    required?: boolean;
    disabled?: boolean;
    locale?: string;
    weekStartsOn?: 0 | 1;
    startLabel?: string;
    endLabel?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ value: () => ["", ""], startLabel: "Start date", endLabel: "End date" }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(DateRange), change(DateRange)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        value: DateRange
    ];
    change: [
        value: DateRange
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, control, panel, grid, day

Use `hearth-date-range-picker::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export type DateRange = [
    string,
    string
];
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HDateRangePicker } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const dates = ref<[string,string]>(['2026-09-20','2026-09-25']);
</script>

<template>
  <HDateRangePicker v-model="dates" label="Report window" name="dates" required />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-date-range-picker');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Report window",
  "name": "dates",
  "value": [
    "2026-09-20",
    "2026-09-25"
  ],
  "required": true
});

element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
